data.summary: Activity on urlquery.net likely attributed to Claude shows attempts to extract information from Amap and (seemingly) to bypass Amap's anti-bot protections
data.description:
update: This activity has also been reported publicly by Swarmchasers: https://swarmcha.se/posts/chinese-agent-fleet

- searching amap.com (a Chinese navigation service) on urlquery.net reveals >2000 reports from 2026-10-04 UTC. Many of the visits covered mention "claude" in the URL.
  - edit: specifically, "claude" appears in a uqscan parameter in about 9% of relevant reports. this parameter could be chosen freely by the actor behind the activity, so this is not conclusive evidence. Thanks Luis for pointing this out!
  - in fact, Swarmchasers presents a case that it's almost certainly not Claude, and plausibly Tencent Hy, by comparing the coding style of the activity to the coding styles of models
- My uncertain read is that the activity is from a batch of Claude-assisted agent runs answering similar questions about Amap, possibly for the purpose of evaluating Claude.
- The activity includes several elaborate strategies, including (a) turning a visit URL into a program that delegates to another browser, (b) making otherwise inaccessible output appear in recorded network requests, and (c) inspecting and manipulating the anti-bot machinery
- Beyond attempts to bypass Amap's anti-bot protections, I found no evidence of a malicious or harmful goal behind the activity.

With help from GPT-6 Astra, I found eight specific reports, linked below, that display evidence of particularly notable strategies. There are likely many more!
